cohortDefinition: 19 listed June 2026 FDA action/goal records, including one CDRH PMA and one generic item with insufficient dated evidence; source list retrieved in Nov after outcomes displayed; not a pre-registered representative sample.
sourceDateCaveat: Source dates taken from press releases, contemporaneous filing dates and registry; original URL byte-versions not independently frozen as of May 31. A registry viewed today can contain later changes.

cases.level1Clinical: 505(b)(2) dexmethylphenidate extended-release formulation seeks once-daily ADHD coverage; clinical efficacy is not a new molecular mechanism.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: March 2026 10-K disclosed February preapproval CMO inspection and Form 483 with three observations, one CTx-1301-specific.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the identified regulatory/manufacturing concern is sufficient for a conservative CRL lean. Independent decision risk: March 2026 10-K disclosed February preapproval CMO inspection and Form 483 with three observations, one CTx-1301-specific.
cases.caveat: May 31 was the original PDUFA goal, so classify as June FDA action, not June original-goal case.

cases.level1Clinical: Known romidepsin pharmacology, but no authenticated pre-June application-specific clinical/bioequivalence and CMC dossier in this review.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Generic CGT ready-to-use formulation could be approved or fail sterility and manufacturing review; lack of filing-specific facts.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: published case-specific evidence is insufficient to assign a defensible FDA direction. Independent decision risk: Generic CGT ready-to-use formulation could be approved or fail sterility and manufacturing review; lack of filing-specific facts.
cases.caveat: Do not manufacture a predecision source or a directional FDA forecast.

cases.level1Clinical: Phase 3 BASIS met annualized bleed-rate endpoint; pediatric BASIS KIDS supportive extension, expanding preapproved antibody.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Marked unmet inhibitor need and regulatory priority review; pediatric sample, development safety and thrombosis remain concerns.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: Marked unmet inhibitor need and regulatory priority review; pediatric sample, development safety and thrombosis remain concerns.
cases.caveat: Exact pediatric population must not be inferred from adult inhibitor results alone.

cases.level1Clinical: Existing licensed IL-13 biologic with published long-term extension supporting durable response every eight weeks.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Smaller injection burden; long-term rescue-treatment data, bias in maintenance cohorts and original SAP remain incomplete.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: Smaller injection burden; long-term rescue-treatment data, bias in maintenance cohorts and original SAP remain incomplete.
cases.caveat: Bridging/label update rather than new-molecule efficacy.

cases.application: KEYTRUDA/QLEX + WELIREG adjuvant clear cell RCC
cases.level1Clinical: Randomized Phase 3 adjuvant ccRCC DFS 28% relative recurrence/death risk reduction vs pembrolizumab alone.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: OS immature; added belzutifan hypoxia/anemia and adjuvant exposure burden compared with existing active regimen.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: OS immature; added belzutifan hypoxia/anemia and adjuvant exposure burden compared with existing active regimen.
cases.caveat: Benefit-risk favorable on prespecified DFS but verify full safety and final hierarchical alpha.

cases.level1Clinical: Phase 3 rPFS HR 0.81, p=.034, modest 7.5-month median gain; immature OS HR .90 p=.401.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: FDA ODAC April 2026 briefing questioned whether rPFS clinical effect was sufficiently meaningful in asymptomatic early mHSPC, and additive toxicity.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the identified regulatory/manufacturing concern is sufficient for a conservative CRL lean. Independent decision risk: FDA ODAC April 2026 briefing questioned whether rPFS clinical effect was sufficiently meaningful in asymptomatic early mHSPC, and additive toxicity.
cases.caveat: Conservative risk lean despite statistically positive primary; this may be a misjudgment if FDA accepts narrower PTEN-deficient indication.

cases.level1Clinical: Bayer FDA-accepted NDA for lower-gadolinium-dose macrocyclic MRI contrast agent across multiple anatomic indications.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: MRI visualization and low dose plausible, but reader validation, gadolinium retention, neonate data and CMC require review.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: MRI visualization and low dose plausible, but reader validation, gadolinium retention, neonate data and CMC require review.
cases.caveat: Source confirms filing rather than original per-reader pivotal numerical results.

cases.application: SKINVIVE by JUVÉDERM neck appearance expansion
cases.level1Clinical: Dermal filler neck-line indication under PMA P110033/S099 (received May 13 2025), NOT a drug NDA/BLA.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Categorically different CDRH device authorization and regulatory rules.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: this is a CDRH PMA device decision and is outside drug PDUFA scoring. Independent decision risk: Categorically different CDRH device authorization and regulatory rules.
cases.caveat: Do not include as drug PDUFA accuracy denominator.

cases.level1Clinical: Phase 3 PIVOT-PO noninferior to imipenem-cilastatin for cUTI; early stopped for efficacy after 1690 participants.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Potential first oral carbapenem with positive trial; resistance stewardship, microbiological eradication, 2022 prior review and CMC outstanding.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: Potential first oral carbapenem with positive trial; resistance stewardship, microbiological eradication, 2022 prior review and CMC outstanding.
cases.caveat: GSK and SPRO represent ONE licensed application; no duplicate case.

cases.level1Clinical: Phase 3 STRIDE-13 positive immunogenicity versus PPSV23 in at-risk ages 2-17, licensed in adults.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Extrapolation of validated OPA immunogenicity; pediatric risk groups, adverse events and vaccine-type interactions require review.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: Extrapolation of validated OPA immunogenicity; pediatric risk groups, adverse events and vaccine-type interactions require review.
cases.caveat: Not two separate approvals for Merck and its licensed pediatric indication.

cases.level1Clinical: Two pivotal randomized Phase 3 studies reported statistically significant smoking abstinence.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Unmet need and repeat positive efficacy support favorable clinical evidence; third-party CMC and final label are not resolved publicly.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: Unmet need and repeat positive efficacy support favorable clinical evidence; third-party CMC and final label are not resolved publicly.
cases.caveat: Approval lean can miss a CMC-only CRL; cannot treat clinical effect as confirmation of manufacturing readiness.

cases.application: IBRANCE palbociclib HER2-positive breast cancer maintenance
cases.level1Clinical: PATINA randomized Phase 3 PFS HR 0.75, p .02 for adding palbociclib to anti-HER2/endocrine maintenance.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Clinical gain on PFS with considerably more grade 3/4 neutropenia; OS and tolerability not fully mature.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: Clinical gain on PFS with considerably more grade 3/4 neutropenia; OS and tolerability not fully mature.
cases.caveat: PFS clinically positive but higher toxicity and lack of OS impose label uncertainty.

cases.application: TRODELVY first-line TNBC mono and KEYTRUDA combo
cases.level1Clinical: ASCENT-03 PFS HR 0.62 p<.0001; companion ASCENT-04 reported favorable PFS in PD-L1-positive population.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Prior metastatic TNBC authorization supports efficacy; neutropenia, diarrhea, OS maturity and indication-specific PD-L1 eligibility unresolved.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: Prior metastatic TNBC authorization supports efficacy; neutropenia, diarrhea, OS maturity and indication-specific PD-L1 eligibility unresolved.
cases.caveat: Two supplemental indications based on related separate pivotal trials, count one listed cohort row.

cases.level1Clinical: Phase 3 CORE/CORE2 sponsor data positive triglyceride reduction, established oligonucleotide already approved in FCS.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Potential pancreatitis prevention meaningful but risk reduction not entirely supported by fully mature event counts; tolerability and liver risk need review.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: Potential pancreatitis prevention meaningful but risk reduction not entirely supported by fully mature event counts; tolerability and liver risk need review.
cases.caveat: Original verified goal June 30; FDA acted earlier June 24.

cases.level1Clinical: Phase 3 pediatric program completed enrollment with adult risankizumab approval precedent and pediatric PK extrapolation; exact predecision efficacy table not independently captured.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Known IL-23 mechanism and durable adult benefit; pediatric dosing, immunogenicity and infection exposure remain important.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: Known IL-23 mechanism and durable adult benefit; pediatric dosing, immunogenicity and infection exposure remain important.
cases.caveat: Current registry may contain post-May changes; no dated original version authenticated.

cases.level1Clinical: Two positive Phase 3 TED studies for proptosis with rapid diplopia improvements and priority review.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Anti-IGF1R effect clinically relevant; hearing-related adverse events, infusion issues and BLA CMC could complicate.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: Anti-IGF1R effect clinically relevant; hearing-related adverse events, infusion issues and BLA CMC could complicate.
cases.caveat: Pre-May source gives June 30 goal; listed approval action occurred earlier.

cases.level1Clinical: Three original clinical studies and accepted Class 2 resubmission; 2025 CRL arose from third-party manufacturing compliance, not efficacy.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Unresolved manufacturing inspection chain is central binary agency risk even with improved tolerability and lower pill burden.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the identified regulatory/manufacturing concern is sufficient for a conservative CRL lean. Independent decision risk: Unresolved manufacturing inspection chain is central binary agency risk even with improved tolerability and lower pill burden.
cases.caveat: No independent proof the original plant deficiency was cleared before the new action.

cases.level1Clinical: Existing topical PDE4 inhibitor pediatric efficacy and safety experience; accepted sNDA extends lower age in psoriasis.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Low systemic exposure and familiar marketed product; careful separation from atopic dermatitis 0.05% regimen is required.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the positive development evidence and known regulatory precedents favor an approval lean, subject to unresolved inspections, labeling and data review. Independent decision risk: Low systemic exposure and familiar marketed product; careful separation from atopic dermatitis 0.05% regimen is required.
cases.caveat: Do not mistake the separate INTEGUMENT-PED dermatitis trial as direct pivotal evidence for 0.3% psoriasis.

cases.application: LNTH-2501 gallium-68 edotreotide NET PET kit
cases.level1Clinical: PET SSTR-targeted diagnostic, with existing chemistry and clinical potential; original diagnostic reader validation not adjudicated.
cases.level2RiskBenefit: Explicit March three-month FDA extension for added manufacturing material makes unresolved third-party CMC credible nonclinical blockage.
cases.level3Regulatory: Regulatory Level 3 judgment: the identified regulatory/manufacturing concern is sufficient for a conservative CRL lean. Independent decision risk: Explicit March three-month FDA extension for added manufacturing material makes unresolved third-party CMC credible nonclinical blockage.
cases.caveat: Class 2 extension isn't a CRL in itself; this is a cautious CMC failure lean.
